canonical.title: Construct Binary Tree from Inorder and Postorder Traversal
canonical.sourceFilePath: 11. Binary Trees/3. Hard/09. Construct BT from inorder and postorder.cpp

narrative.title: Rewinding the Warehouse Shutdown Log
narrative.scenario: A shutdown audit captured two walks of a conveyor tree: a leaves-first log (each junction written after everything beneath it) and a left-first inventory. Junction names never repeat, so reading the leaves-first log backwards always names the next junction, and the left-first inventory reveals exactly how many conveyors feed each side of it.
narrative.inputFormat: Two integer arrays — inorder (left subtree, root, right subtree) and postorder (left subtree, right subtree, root) of the same tree. Values are unique.
narrative.outputFormat: Return the constructed binary tree serialized as a level-order array (null marks a missing child, trailing nulls trimmed).

testCases.explanation: The last postorder value 3 is the root; 9 hangs left, and 20 roots the right subtree over 15 and 7.
1 closes the postorder, so it is the root; 2 and 3 split as its left and right children.

hintLevels: Level 1: Postorder ends with the root — read it backwards and the current root always comes first.
Level 2: Locate that root in the inorder array; its left fragment sizes the left subtree in the postorder walk.
Level 3: Peel postorder from the back and build right before left — the right subtree's nodes sit just before the root.
